prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's density relaxation is a single global scalar, but the TNS cost is driven by *regional* density spikes in the hottest bins; instead of further loosening the global weight, cap the per-bin density weight growth (`density_weight_new`) more tightly in the late stage so hot regions cannot explode and displace critical cells, while leaving the global ramp untouched — this stabilizes TNS without weakening wirelength/timing pressure elsewhere.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.592 robust(mean-std)=+0.178 min_case=+0.171 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.171 dWNS=+10.5% dTNS=+22.0% overflow~103
  bp-ng45: score=+0.205 dWNS=+20.5% dTNS=+20.7% overflow~136
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.217 dWNS=+8.1% dTNS=+31.0% overflow~177
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis holds: capping late-stage per-bin density weight growth improved TNS across all three cases (dTNS +20.7% to +31.0%) with WNS also improving, and no invalid runs. The mechanism is consistent with regional density spikes being contained, freeing critical cells from displacement—bp_fe-ng45 shows the largest TNS gain (+31.0%) despite modest WNS (+8.1%), suggesting reduced hot-bin congestion rather than global loosening. Next step: sweep the cap value (e.g., tighter vs. current) on bp_fe-ng45 and ariane133-ng45 to find the knee where TNS gains saturate before WNS or wirelength degrades.
